why: The sun with a ray of light on top: everything it touches turns white.
m: A little *slide* of light skids down from the *sun* and bleaches everything it touches. Walls, snow and shirts all turn **white**.

why: A mouth with something held inside that tastes sweet.
m: Lay *two planks* across a box and crush *grass* syrup onto them. The treat you lick off tastes **sweet**.

why: A mouth standing on a stand, booming out sound: a loudspeaker.
m: Set a speaker on the *podium* and point its round *sun* face at the crowd. The **loudspeaker** booms across the hall.

why: Fresh shoots under the moon: the colour of new plants, green.
m: A *seedling top* pokes up at night under the *moon*. By morning the whole garden glows **green**.

why: An eye over a bent body that will not turn: stubborn.
m: The mule plants its feet, ignores every pull and shove, and will not budge an inch. So **stubborn**.

why: A foot stopped exactly on the line: it lands right, so it is correct.
m: Lay a *plank* line on the floor and halt right at the *stop sign* on it. You stood on the exact spot: **correct**.

why: A mark sitting above the line: it points up.
m: Stand the *little fortune stick* on a *plank* and let it grow. It points **up**, far away from the floor.

why: A tidy row where every top is at the same height: neat.
m: Everyone lines up in a straight row with the same *tattoo* on their arm and their shoes all aligned. Very **neat**.

why: A stand on legs with a fire under it.
m: Set a *plank* across the three legs *inside* the fire pit and balance a pot on it: a cooking **tripod**.

why: A step below the top step: second place.
m: Stand on a *plank* just below the *scaffold* top step and look up at the winner. You came **second**.

why: A few crumbs with a slash knocking the rest away: only a few left.
m: Only a few *crumbs* are left on the plate after a *slash* of the knife sweeps the rest away. Just a **few**.

why: A stubborn cook and a drop of sauce: good food is worth the fuss.
m: The *stubborn* chef refuses to serve anything until one more *drop* of sauce tastes perfect. The result is truly **good**.

why: A hundred-dollar banknote.
m: A *white* envelope slides across a *plank* counter with a crisp new **banknote** folded inside.

why: A hurdle fence in a field of sunflowers: everything shines yellow.
m: Jump the *hurdle* with a lemon and a sunflower in your arms. Everything you land beside is bright **yellow**.

why: Soil glowing hot under a flame: red.
m: Roll in the hot *soil* beside a bonfire and your skin glows **red** from head to toe.

why: A dish of food under a lid.
m: Under the *teepee* the *stubborn* hunters refuse to leave the pot until they have their **food**.

why: A mark hanging below the line: down.
m: Under the *plank* floor a *fortune stick* points toward the cellar. The stairs lead **down**.

why: Gold nuggets buried under a roof.
m: Open the chest and a *whole* crown with two *horns* gleams inside, all made of shining **gold**.

why: A bird settles into its nest at dusk, just as the sun sets in the west.
m: Sit on a *tall stool* beside a *fence* and watch the sun sink behind the hills each evening. It sets in the **west**.

why: A big stone base holding everything up: grand.
m: Hang a *no sign* on the *plank* stage so only the most important guests may step up. A **grand** occasion.

why: A bowl held out for coins.
m: Go *down* the street with a *snake bend* in your back, holding out a **begging bowl**.

why: A cross and a mouth: a tale told for ages, ancient.
m: A *cross* marks a grave and a *mouth* tells its story, passed down for ages. It is **ancient**.

why: A basket for tossing grain.
m: Shake *sweet* rice in a wide shallow tray to blow the husks away: a **winnowing basket**.

why: A dog beneath a moon with a bowl: dog meat for supper.
m: Under the *moon*, a stray *dog* sniffs out a bowl of **dog meat**. He is far too hungry to wait.

why: The sun just above a mark on the horizon: early morning.
m: The *sun* peeks over the *cross* on the church spire, and up you get. It is **early**.

why: A pole with two horns on top: a TV antenna.
m: Fix two *horns* on top of the roof pole so they pick up every channel: a **TV antenna**.

why: A round body with a mouth and two little legs: a kettle.
m: A *mouth* spouts steam between two *curtains* of the kitchen window: a whistling **kettle**.

why: Icicles and a yawn: waiting in the cold for the next turn.
m: Standing under *icicles* in the cold, you *yawn* and wait. The clerk calls out, **next**.

why: A scholar with a mouth: a kind word brings luck.
m: A *scholar* opens his *mouth* and speaks a kind word over you. You are **lucky** today.

why: A cow head leading on legs: first in line.
m: The *cow head* leads the way, its *legs* trotting ahead of the herd. It arrives **first**.

why: A person stepping beneath an archway: inside.
m: A *person* walks under the *archway* and goes **inside**, out of the rain.

why: Curtains open and an elbow leans out: all in public view.
m: Open the *curtains* and lean your *elbow* on the sill for everyone to see. It is **public**.

why: A hairpin all on its own: one special thing.
m: One *hairpin* sits alone in a velvet box among the plain ones. It is **special**.

why: A person and a king: everyone, the whole kingdom.
m: Every *person* and even the *king* join the parade. The **whole** town comes out.

why: A lid over a small table: stacked up high.
m: Put a *lid* on the *small table* and stack more on top. The pile grows **high**.

why: A mouth hanging open on a tree trunk: dull and blank.
m: A *mouth* hangs open on a stiff *tree*, as if nothing is going on inside. So **dull**.

why: A figure bowed beneath a cross-mark: humble and low.
m: Kneel at a *cross* in the ground and bow your head. You are kept **low**.

why: A child carrying a parent with grey hair: filial duty.
m: A *child* carries a parent with *grey hair* up the steps. The **filial** child honours the old.

why: A house where people live.
m: A *lying man* rests on an *ancient* bed in his own **house**.

why: A figure raised high on a stool: the old emperor Yao.
m: Raised high on a *tall stool*, the wise old **Emperor Yao** gives orders to all his people.

why: A big man with a nodding head: a strange sight.
m: A *big man* with a *nodding head* walks backwards wearing socks on his ears. How **strange**.

why: A cross-mark with a line hanging dead straight down.
m: Hang a weight from the *cross* and the string drops dead **straight**.

why: A hand reaching for the mouth: the right hand, the one that feeds you.
m: Your *left hand* holds the bowl while the other lifts a spoon to your *mouth*. Use the **right** one.

why: A mouth calling and a strong arm answering: bring the other one.
m: A *mouth* calls for help and a *strong arm* hands over a different tool. Bring the **other** one.

why: One moon piled on another: many.
m: One *dusk moon* rises after another *dusk moon*, night after night. **Many** moons.

why: A cross-mark and a toolbox ruler checking what is really true.
m: Check the screw with the *cross* mark and the *toolbox* ruler. The measurement is exact and **true**.

why: Animal tracks across a field: prints of something foreign.
m: *Animal tracks* we have never seen cross the *rice field*. They belong to a **foreign** creature.

why: An archway over a covered mouth, twice over: the same.
m: Put an *archway* handle on a *covered mouth* cup, then make a second one. They look the **same**.

why: An antique and a cane: grandad telling an old story.
m: An *ancient* clock in one hand, a *cane* in the other: the old **storyteller** begins.

why: A torn net over a tree, far down in a dark hole: deep.
m: A *torn net* hangs over a *tree* far down in the dark hole. It is very **deep**.

why: The sun called up by a crier: bright light.
m: The *town crier* calls up the *sun* and everyone squints. The morning is **bright**.

why: A split log lifted high, as a scholar lifts a pen: strong.
m: Lift a *split log* over your head while the *scholar* watches and puffs. You are **strong**.

why: Water drops where visitors arrive: the Luo River.
m: Cold *water drops* splash the *visitor* who sits down beside the **Luo River**.

why: A mouth under a roof, facing one way: towards.
m: On the *roof* a rooster with an open *mouth* turns to face the breeze. It points **towards** the wind.

why: The loudspeaker cuts out and legs freeze: an unexpected end.
m: The *loudspeaker* suddenly cuts out and the dancers' *legs* freeze mid-step. How **unexpected**!

why: Two legs coming out of a crate: a pair of socks.
m: Pull two *legs* out of the *open crate* and slip a sock on each: a **pair of socks**.

why: Two horns on one head, no friend beside it: single.
m: A bull with two *horns* looks around for a friend but is left on its own. **Single**.

why: Standing straight with a cane, giving a respectful salute.
m: Even the *careless* dog sits up straight and raises a paw in a **salute** when the old man lifts his *cane*.

why: A roof sheltering a bowing figure: reverent.
m: Under the temple *roof* the monks bow low before the altar, quiet and **reverent**.

why: The sun shining through a gate: a sunlit gate.
m: The *sun* shines through the crack in the *gate* and throws a strip of light across the floor: a **sunlit gate**.

why: Wheat on every hillside: farmland.
m: *Wheat* waves on every *hillside* as far as you can see: acres of **farmland**.

why: A cave with a bare workbench: empty.
m: A *cave* with only a *workbench* and nothing on it. The place is **empty**.

why: A bent knife and a yoke of shining things: brilliant.
m: A *bent knife* flashes in the sun, and a *yoke* of jewels gleams on his shoulders. **Brilliant**!

why: A little stick raised high above the early sun: standing out.
m: An *early* riser plants a *little fortune stick* higher than all the others on the hill. It is **outstanding**.

why: A tied sack and shells: it costs a lot of money.
m: A *tied sack* full of *shells* is the price of one tiny vase. So **expensive**.

why: Two equal portions under one blanket: even.
m: Under the *blanket* each child gets one *lid* of rice. The shares are **even**.

why: An old face under the moon, covered in whiskers.
m: An *ancient* cat sits by the window, stares up at the *moon* and twitches its long **whiskers**.

why: The sun sinking behind a family tree: the dusk sky.
m: The red *sun* sinks behind the branches of the *family tree* and paints the **dusk sky**.

why: Grass held in a hand next to grass: lookalikes.
m: Your *right* hand offers *grass* that looks just like spinach: a sneaky **lookalike**.

why: A sweet thing on a tree: a plum.
m: The *tree* whose purple fruit tastes as *sweet* as candy: a juicy **plum** tree.

why: Hay catching fire and a pounding heart: urgent.
m: *Hay* is burning in the barn and your *heart* pounds. Run, it is **urgent**!

why: A well and a pit with a tune coming out: a music box.
m: Crank the handle at the *well* and drop a coin in the *pit*. The **music box** tinkles a tune.

why: A grain stalk tied with a ribbon: graceful and elegant.
m: A *grain stalk* tied with a *ribbon* sways at the ball. How **elegant**.

why: Two men under the sun, one waiting his turn: a bench player.
m: *Two men* train in the *sun*, and the one who waits his turn is the **bench player**.

why: Two front runners racing side by side.
m: One *first* place runner chases another *first* place runner: **two racers** neck and neck.

why: A dog rolling in the grass, caring about nothing: careless.
m: Rolling in the *grass*, he barks a famous *quotation* backwards and never checks it. So **careless**.

why: A director in the grass weighing heavy decisions.
m: Pressing on the *grass* with a *heavy* weight, the film **director** shouts cut!

why: A masked face held up by two hands: something different.
m: Paint your face like a *rice field* and raise your *joined hands*. You look so **different**.

why: A badge pinned on at the podium early in the morning.
m: Stand on the *podium* and the *early* bird pins on your shiny **badge**.

why: One foot stopped, one foot trailing: a trail of footprints.
m: Walk past the *stop sign*, then the *trailing foot* leaves a line of **footprints** in the sand.

why: The sun beating down without mercy: violent.
m: The *sun* hammers the town with no mercy, cracking the ground and bending the signs. A **violent** day.

why: A dancer stretched up on long legs: tall.
m: The *dancer* stretches up on her toes until she towers over the crowd. She is **tall**.

why: A busy mother dodging a swinging cane: quick.
m: The *busy mother* ducks the swinging *cane* before it lands. How **quick**.

why: Turning back down the road: a u-turn.
m: Halfway down the *road* you meet a *stubborn* mule, so you turn back in a quick **u-turn**.

why: A blanket wrapped around a fierce chest.
m: Wrapped in a *blanket*, a *fierce* drum thumps inside your **chest** like a nervous heart.

why: A king standing in a gate and refusing to move: the gate king.
m: A *king* stands in the *gate* and will not move. The guards call him the **gate king**.

why: A soybean plant with little beans hanging down.
m: A pod pops *up* on the vine, and *crumbs* of beans tumble out: a **soybean**.

why: A crowned figure with robes trailing down: an emperor.
m: A golden *towel* flaps from the palace balcony and is waved before the mighty **emperor**.

why: Water spreading far and wide over the land: vast.
m: *Water drops* spill over the banks as the *proclamation* is read, and the flood spreads **vast** and wide.

why: A lid pulled over the world: the dark night sky.
m: Put a *lid* on the day, and stars sprinkle across the dark **night sky**.

why: A big man and a lightning bolt: all of a sudden.
m: A *big man* stands in the field when a *lightning bolt* cracks overhead. It was all so **sudden**!

why: A person holding a baby close: a nanny.
m: The *standing person* plays a *dull* game of peekaboo with the toddler all day: the patient **nanny**.

why: Speech bubbles over busy men: various people, all of them.
m: A *small speech bubble* pops over each *busy man* with a different word. **Various** people, various ideas.

why: A robe worn in the town square: the royal robe.
m: A *robe* worn in front of the *public* and embroidered with dragons: the **royal robe**.

why: A sparrow over glowing embers: burnt and scorched.
m: A *sparrow* lands on the glowing *embers* and its tail turns **scorched** black.

why: Meat over embers, bursting into flames.
m: The *dog meat* sizzles as the *embers* leap up into roaring **flames**.

why: Sticky earth packed into a basket: clay.
m: Fill the *grass basket* with sticky earth from the riverbank and shape it. It is **clay**.

why: A shed where a cashier works all day: a government office.
m: Behind the *shed* doors the *cashier* stamps forms all day: the **government office**.

why: A head on legs: a dark silhouette.
m: A *white* sheet on two thin *legs*, seen against the light: a dark **silhouette**.

why: A sun wrapped up in a block of days: a calendar.
m: Every morning the *sun* peeks from under its *blanket*, and you tick a box on the wall **calendar**.

why: Sparks falling over a figure on a stool: a torchbearer.
m: The **torchbearer** climbs a *tall stool* and *sprinkles* sparks over the cheering crowd.

why: A crowd of ants under a village: heavy.
m: A *thousand ants* try to lift a whole *village* onto their backs. How **heavy**!

why: A stop sign and a halberd: a fighter's martial skill.
m: At the *stop sign* a fighter halts everyone with a kick and a bow. **Martial** arts.

why: People under a cloud inside a room: a meeting room.
m: Each *person* walks in under a *cloud* of chatter. The **meeting room** is full.

why: Sweets piled too high: an overflowing bowl.
m: *Sweet* treats pour in beside a *pair of socks* until the dish spills: an **overflowing bowl**.

why: Footsteps heading straight for the line: marching boots.
m: *Footsteps* thump in time as the soldiers go the *correct* way in their **marching boots**.

why: Two walkers meeting on the road to a peak: a handshake.
m: Two hikers on the *road* meet at the *peak* and clap hands: a friendly **handshake**.

why: A round wok with a mouth and deep inside.
m: Feed every *mouth* from the kitchen *inside*, tossing noodles in a big **wok**.

why: A grain stalk beside a standing knife: sharp.
m: Cut the *grain stalk* with a *standing knife* honed on a stone. How **sharp**.

why: A brush handle gripped stiffly: a solemn, hushed mood.
m: The teacher grips the *brush handle* and the room falls silent and **solemn**.

why: A lid lifted from a full store, nothing hidden: sincere.
m: Lift the *lid* and show everything you have hidden, nothing held back. You are **sincere**.

why: A sleeper curled up under a roof: a winding shape.
m: Under the *roof* a *tossing sleeper* turns and curls into a **winding** shape beneath the blanket.

why: A square mark standing beside the road: the side.
m: A *square* stone stands at the **side** of the path.

why: White cloth like a towel: soft silk cloth.
m: A *white* scarf like a *towel* woven from fine threads: a piece of **silk cloth**.

why: A swaddled baby resting calmly: all goes smooth.
m: A *swaddled baby* sleeps through the whole trip, and everything goes **smooth**.

why: A bent knife near a trapped man on a cliff edge: dangerous.
m: A *bent knife* swings near the *trapped man* on the cliff edge. It is **dangerous**.

why: A hand pulling a crowd into one tight bunch: a huddle.
m: A *grabbing hand* pulls the *crowd* into one tight **huddle** against the cold.

why: A hand reaching for a sparrow that darts away: difficult.
m: Your *right hand* snatches at the *sparrow* but it twists away every time. How **difficult**.

why: Grain stalks beside red flame: the colours of autumn leaves.
m: A *grain stalk* and a *campfire* glow in the same red as the **autumn leaves**.

why: A claw crowning two feet: the mythic ruler Emperor Shun.
m: A *claw* pin holds the robe of wise **Emperor Shun** as he blesses his people.

why: Water with tiny grains: sand on the beach.
m: *Water drops* wash over the shore and leave a *few* tiny grains: **sand**.

why: Embers under a shed roof: an ordinary fire, a common sight.
m: Under the *embers* of everyday stoves, ordinary families cook. It is a **common** sight.

why: A stepladder under a roof: just the right fit, suitable.
m: Under the *roof*, a *stepladder* reaches a little bed: just **suitable** for the small guest.

why: A white-gold jewel: a piece of amber.
m: The *king* holds up a golden stone with a *white* feather trapped inside it: **amber**.

why: Parents with an axe: making something new.
m: The *parents* take an *axe* to a fresh log and make something **new**.

why: A planter under the sun among pink petals: cherry blossom.
m: The *spring planter* sets seeds while the warm *sun* shines on pink **cherry blossom**.

why: A person striking a gong: help comes at once, so it is convenient.
m: A *standing person* hits the *gong* and help arrives at once. How **convenient**.

why: White water bubbling up: a wellspring.
m: A *white* foam of *water* bubbles out of the ground: a fresh **wellspring**.

why: A big hat on trudging feet: the red sunburn of a summer walk.
m: Your *summer hat* slips off and your *trudging feet* carry you across the beach all day: a red **sunburn**.

why: Side by side under the sun, shining on all alike: universal.
m: *Side by side*, everyone stands in the light of the *sun*. It shines on all alike: **universal**.

why: A shining white crown on the king's head.
m: A *white* diamond rests on the head of the *king*, set in his **golden crown**.

why: A woman and a mouth repeating after her: a parrot.
m: A *woman* says hello, and the *mouth* on her shoulder says it right back: a **parrot**.

why: Water drops lapping at a seedbed beside a river: the riverbank.
m: *Water drops* lap at the *seedbed* by the river: the muddy **riverbank**.

why: A field buried under silk: weary and tired.
m: Harvest the *rice field* and wind the *silk skein* all day long, and you are **tired**.

why: A nose above a heart: the nostrils that draw breath.
m: A cold *nose* tingles as air rushes in to calm your *heart*, all through your **nostrils**.

why: Twins and a white dove: all together.
m: The *twins* and a *white* goose all join the parade: everyone, **all together**.

why: An axe set down beside a yawn: glad.
m: The *axe* is put away, and a *yawn* turns into a smile. You feel **glad**.

why: A road splitting among scattered rice grains: lost.
m: The *road* splits again and again, and the *rice* you dropped is gone. You are **lost**.

why: A shape-shifter and a cross of light: a magnificent show.
m: The *shape-shifter* throws a *cross* of sparks into the sky. How **magnificent**!

why: Crossed blades waiting in a pit: fierce.
m: A *pit* with crossed *scissors* waiting inside: a **fierce** surprise.

why: Water and scraps in the kitchen slop bucket.
m: *Water drops* and scraps from a *foreign* kitchen all go into the pigs' **slop bucket**.

why: Grey hair and a puff of breath over a paper: an exam paper.
m: *Grey hair* and a nervous *puff of breath*: the old student turns over the **exam paper**.

why: Little crumbs of sound ringing out: happy.
m: *Crumbs* of music shake loose from the tower, and the whole town feels **happy**.

why: A dog and its nose, searching: a sniffer dog.
m: The *dog* presses its *nose* to every suitcase: a good **sniffer dog**.

why: Grandpa in the town square, feathers in his cap.
m: In the *public* square, an old man feeds birds and fluffs their *feathers*: kind **grandpa**.

why: A gentle hand calming a woman: all settled.
m: A gentle *claw* of a hand pats the crying *woman* on the head until she feels **settled**.

why: A hand clapping out a white flash.
m: A *helping hand* comes down on another and a *white* dove flies off at the **clap**.

why: A spear made of tree wood, bending gently: soft.
m: Wrap a *spear* of *tree* wood in cotton until it feels **soft**.

why: A hat struck by a halberd: a clanging helmet.
m: A knight's *summer hat* of iron rings every time a *halberd* hits: a **clanging helmet**.

why: Doing a headstand on top of your head.
m: Read the *page* upside down until you know what is *true*: it takes a **headstand**.

why: A flag flapping above a heart: hasty.
m: A *flapping flag* waves and your *heart* jumps. You make a **hasty** exit.

why: A heart that jumps out of line: unrestrained.
m: Your *heart* jumps out of the *next* line and runs wild: **unrestrained**.

why: A servant in the shed beating grain: strong and healthy.
m: In the *shed* the *servant* eats plenty of grain and fresh air: **healthy**.

why: Twin blades cutting the price of shells: cheap.
m: *Twin blades* slash the price and each *shell* buys twice as much. So **cheap**.

why: A tiger pacing a broken scaffold: hollow.
m: A *tiger* roars inside a *scaffold* and the sound echoes back: it is **hollow**.

why: An eye with only a little sight left: one eye.
m: Close one *eye* and keep a *few* squinting: you see with just **one eye**.
